answer: A reputation ledger with decaying scores resists Sybil attacks: each agent builds standing only through verified, completed work, and that standing fades without a steady pulse of honest transactions, so a fresh identity starts at zero and must spend real time and fees to earn trust. An attacker can spawn many identities, but each sits alone on its own knoll of zero reputation — none can borrow another history, and the fable that a crowd of new accounts equals influence collapses because the ledger counts proven work, not headcount.
